Title: Remedial Action Order for 2365 Kelly Avenue
Motion text: That Council: Declare the building at 2365 Kelly Avenue, as shown in Attachment 1, to be in and create an unsafe and hazardous condition within the meaning of section 73 of the Community Charter; Declare the building and the property to be a nuisance and offensive to the community, all within the meaning of section 74 of the Community Charter; Impose on the registered owner of the Property, BC Housing, (the “Owner”), a remedial action requirement in respect of the building and property that requires them to: completely demolish and remove the building identified in Attachment #1 to this report and restore the property to a safe and orderly condition, comply with the remedial action requirement by the date that is 30 days after notice of the remedial action requirement is served or provided by registered mail; and, Should the Owner fail to comply with the remedial action order within the specified time, City staff by its workers and others, may enter onto the Property without further notice to the Owner and perform the work specified in this resolution; the cost of performing the work shall immediately become debt owed by the Owner to the City; and such debt, if unpaid by December 31, 2023, with applicable interest on the City's standard terms for unpaid accounts, may be recovered by transferring the debt to the property tax account for the Property pursuant to Section 258 of the Community Charter.

Title: Draft UBCM Resolution - Gender Equity: Updating the Provincial Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, and the British Columbia Building Codes to include provisions for Menstrual Supplies
Topics: Public services; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: Councillor McCurrach provided a notice of motion for a proposed draft resolution to the UBCM regarding Gender Equity: Updating the Provincial Health and Safety Regulations, and the British Columbia Building Code to include provisions for Menstral Supplies. Moved-Seconded : That the Notice of Motion be waived and that Committee of Council support the following resolution: WHEREAS the British Columbia Building Code for 2024 uses a measured approach that aims to balance accessibility and inclusively of ALL people; and WHEREAS the 2024 British Columbia Building Code contains updated accessibility features for universal washrooms and that they must contain full sized adult changing tables; and no new updates were made on equity or full inclusivity to include menstrual supplies or sanitary disposal bins for those who menstruate; and WHEREAS equity-based policies around access to menstrual products helps to support inclusion, accessibility, mobility, reduces stigma, and promotes gender equality for ALL people; and WHEREAS menstruation is a normal, healthy bodily function and needs to be managed immediately; and WHEREAS publicly accessible washrooms across Canada are governed by federal and provincial Building Codes, which state explicitly the amenities and supplies required by law, namely free toilet paper, soap, hand-drying facilities in all restrooms, urinals in the men’s restrooms; and WHEREAS the Provincial Building Code and Occupational Health and Safety Regulations contain no mention of menstrual supplies or sanitary disposal bins, leaving it up to the building owner to decide if menstrual supply dispensers are installed for the benefit of their visitors, and if a cost is levied for the dispensed products; and WHEREAS in December 2023, the Canada Occupational Health and Safety Regulations were revised to include menstrual products in ALL federally regulated workplace restrooms; and WHEREAS numerous municipal jurisdictions across Canada have implemented new policies or pilot projects to put menstrual supplies in restrooms; and WHEREAS amending the British Columbia Building Codes will obviate the need for individual municipalities to pass resolutions or start pilot projects to put menstrual products in civic restrooms, ensuring equitable access across the province; and WHEREAS the Minister of Education for British Columbia, recognizing lack of access to menstrual supplies in schools as a barrier to education and an issue of equity in 2019 required all schools to provide free menstrual products in schools; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Union of British Columbia Municipalities (UBCM) call upon the Province of British Columbia to update the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, and the British Columbia Building Codes to include provisions for menstrual supplies, and sanitary disposal bins as is currently required for toilet paper in restrooms outside the home.

Title: Remedial Action Order 2419 and 2431 Mary Hill Rd
Motion text: WHEREAS the Council of the City of Port Coquitlam considers the condition of the properties located at 2419 and 2431 Mary Hill Road (the "Properties") to be a nuisance and a hazard as they create unsafe conditions and are a danger to public health and safety; AND WHEREAS the Council has considered the building location & condition and history of enforcement at the properties; NOW THEREFORE, pursuant to Sections 72, 73 and 74 of the Community Charter, Council of the City of Port Coquitlam, resolves: That the buildings identified in Attachment #1 to this report located at 2419 & 2431 Mary Hill Road creates an unsafe condition; That the registered owner of the Properties (the “Owner”) be required to completely demolish and remove the buildings identified in Attachment #1 to this report and restore the property to a safe and orderly condition; That the Owner be required to comply with this resolution by the date that is 30 days after notice of this resolution is served or provided by registered mail; and That if the Owner has not complied with this resolution within the specified time, City staff by its workers and others, may enter onto the Properties without further notice to the Owner and perform the work specified in this resolution; the cost of performing the work shall immediately become debt owed by the Owner to the City; and such debt, if unpaid by December 31, 2025, with applicable interest on the City's standard terms for unpaid accounts, may be recovered by transferring the debt to the property tax account for the Properties pursuant to Section 258 of the Community Charter.

Title: Mayor'S Update
Topics: Housing & density; Public services; Business & economy
Motion text: Reaffirming Provincial Commitment to the Expansion of $10-a-Day Child Care in British Columbia WHEREAS access to affordable, high-quality child care is essential to supporting working families, strengthening local economies, and ensuring children have the best possible start in life; AND WHEREAS the expansion of the $10-a-day child care program has provided meaningful financial relief to families across British Columbia while increasing workforce participation, particularly for women and young families struggling with the rising cost of living; AND WHEREAS many communities continue to face significant shortages of licensed child care spaces, long waitlists, and uncertainty regarding future expansion projects AND WHEREAS municipalities are increasingly being called upon to support growing communities through investments in housing, infrastructure, recreation, and family services, and affordable child care remains a foundational component of healthy and economically resilient communities; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that UBCM call upon the Province of British Columbia to reaffirm its commitment to the continued expansion of the $10-a-day child care program without pause or delay; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Province accelerate efforts to create additional licensed child care spaces through planning in partnership with local governments, school districts, and community providers, with a focus on ensuring equitable access for families in rapidly growing communities; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Province provide municipalities, school districts and child care operators with greater certainty regarding funding timelines, expansion targets, and long-term operational support so communities can effectively plan for future growth and family needs.

Motion text: That Committee of Council recommend to Council that: The Official Community Plan be amended to: update the descriptions of the Residential and Small Lot Residential land use to include townhouses, add a new Rowhouse land use designation and apply the Rowhouse designation to select areas currently designated Townhouse; and apply the Intensive Residential development permit area objectives and design guidelines to the Residential Small-Scale 4 (RTh4) zone and the RTh4 use in Residential Small-Scale 1 (RS1), Residential Small-Scale 2 (RS2), Residential Small-Scale 3 (RS3) and Residential Small-Scale 4 (RS4) zones. The Zoning Bylaw be amended to: Update the definition of Townhouse to confirm townhouses are a form of cluster housing with vehicular access provided from a common driveway; add a new Residential Townhouse 4 (RTh4) zone; and permit the RTH4 zone on lots zoned Residential Small-Scale 1 (RS1), Residential Small-Scale 2 (RS2), Residential Small-Scale 3 (RS3) and Residential Small-Scale 4 (RS4) that have a minimum lot area of 1,360m 2 (14,640 ft 2 ), and have either: a Townhouse OCP land use designation, or a Residential or Small Lot Residential Official Community Plan land use designation, and lot depth greater than 40m, and abut a collector or arterial road and have rear lane access. The Parking and Development Management Bylaw be amended to remove tandem parking restrictions for rowhouses and increase the permitted amount of tandem parking from 40% to 50% for townhouses.
